project.title: Work-to-Portfolio Pipeline
project.summary: A workflow that captures development evidence, uses AI to assemble Work Reports, and turns reviewed material into public portfolio pages.

preview.description: Illustrated overview of evidence moving through capture, AI-assisted Work Reports, human curation in Portfolio Editor, and publication to Portfolio Site.

blocks.body:
## Turn completed work into something people can understand

Completed work leaves evidence scattered across commits, screenshots, terminal sessions, and generated files. Reconstructing that work later means finding the material again and remembering why the decisions mattered.

I built Portfolio Pipeline to connect evidence capture, structured reporting, page composition, and publication. My work spans the handoffs between these stages: preserving artifacts, carrying their context into Work Reports, mapping useful material into editable blocks, and reviewing the page that Portfolio Site will render.

Artifact Pipeline, Work Report, Portfolio Editor, and Portfolio Site provide the four components. This project brings them together as one repeatable workflow.

blocks.description: Evidence moves through capture, structured reporting, page composition, and exact Site review. Owner acceptance precedes the separate publication step.

blocks.body:
## 1. Capture evidence close to the work

Artifact Pipeline collects outputs from development and visual tools, including source changes, screenshots, diagrams, terminal sessions, recordings, and generated files. Records retain the connection between each artifact and the operation that produced it.

Work Report copies selected evidence into durable storage. A useful work record can therefore outlive a temporary output folder or the session that created it. The examples below are artifacts retained with the report behind this page.

blocks.label: Work Evidence Pipeline — capture and provenance

blocks.body:
## 2. Assemble a structured Work Report

Work Report brings the selected evidence together with the description, reasoning, tags, and development context. AI helps synthesize these inputs into a draft that can be checked against its attached artifacts.

The report behind this project page gathers architecture notes, a captured source change, and images of the pipeline's inputs and interfaces. It supplies both the technical account and the material from which the public explanation is composed.

blocks.description: The Work Report behind Portfolio Pipeline retains its architecture account, reasoning, and 19 attached artifacts as source material for the project page.

blocks.label: Work Report System — structured records and retained evidence

blocks.body:
## 3. Compose the public page

Portfolio Editor places source reports beside the rendered page. Its Reports, Pages, and Blocks views support selecting evidence, rewriting the title and summary, arranging the explanation, and connecting the page to projects, capabilities, or milestones.

Browser and agent edits share a revisioned Workspace with autosave and undo. Text, images, galleries, code, diagrams, and other blocks let the page use the form that best explains each claim. The preview uses Portfolio Site's renderer as the page takes shape.

blocks.description: Portfolio Pipeline in the block editor: the palette and ordered page structure sit beside the rendered project overview.

blocks.label: Portfolio Editor — page composition and review

blocks.body:
## 4. Review and publish the selected result

Review project asks Portfolio Site to validate and build the exact proposed page. The owner can inspect its content, assets, and connection changes before accepting that version.

Acceptance prepares the reviewed content for the site. Constellation handles the separate publication step. The public build contains the selected narrative and evidence. The reporting and authoring tools retain the supporting private context.

blocks.description: A saved working page is ready for Review project, which builds the exact candidate for owner inspection.

blocks.label: Portfolio Site — validation, rendering, and public pages

blocks.body:
## Keep evidence, authorship, and publication distinct

I designed the stages to retain different kinds of context. Capture preserves useful work outputs. Reports organize their meaning. The editor selects what a visitor needs to see. The site renders that selected representation.

AI assists with synthesis; I retain responsibility for checking claims, choosing evidence, and shaping the explanation. Autosave preserves that work as it develops, while exact review fixes the content and assets being considered for acceptance. Publication follows that editorial decision.

These boundaries also keep the components useful independently: Work Report can preserve work without creating a portfolio page, and Portfolio Editor can author a page without importing a report.

## What the pipeline delivers

The result is a reusable path from completed work to a public explanation. Evidence remains attached to its source, reports retain technical context, and the editor turns selected material into pages with an explicit review boundary.

The retained artifacts and source account come from the Work Report behind this page. Alongside them, the editor views show how that material is composed into a project overview with a focused narrative, selected visuals, and links to its components and milestones.

The project timeline records how those pieces came together, from the reporting tool and portfolio site through artifact capture, block mapping, and provenance checks.
